in_text_mentions: Examination of the histological images detailed multiple areas of true gyral fusion between adjacent molecular layers, with evidence of entrapped but otherwise normal, leptomeningeal blood vessels (Figure 3). Additionally, a mild decrease in cortical thickness, with focal neuronal loss in the superficial layers and neuronal dyslamination of the neocortex, was noted. No neuronal heterotopias or dysplastic neurons were noted, and pial surfaces demonstrated no specific abnormalities.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows general cortical abnormalities with mis-location and mis-configuration of sulci and gyri in the parietal and right frontal lobes, consistent with polymicrogyria. B: Panel B displays numerous small gyri in the parietal lobes and Sylvian fissure regions bilaterally, which is a classic radiological finding of polymicrogyria. C: Panel C shows misplacement of gyri in the right temporal lobe, specifically the medium temporal gyrus hiding the superior temporal gyrus, indicating cortical malformation.
